title: Apollo 8 - CSM 103
_comment: Apollo 8, the first flight to the Moon: the CSM alone, the S-IVB carrying a test article (LTA-B) where later flights carried the LM, ten lunar orbits, and home. Sources: the Apollo 8 Mission Report (MSC-PA-R-69-1), the Saturn V launch vehicle flight evaluation report for AS-503 (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1) and the Apollo Flight Journal's transcript. Distances in km, times in GET seconds or hhh:mm:ss (GET counts from range zero, 12:51:00 UTC on 21 December 1968).

call_signs._comment: Apollo 8's spacecraft had no call sign of its own: CAPCOM called it Apollo 8 (Apollo Flight Journal) [published]

start_calls.launch: 20 seconds, all aspects we are still Go at this time.
start_calls.translunar_coast: {csm}, Houston. Good trajectory. Your separation maneuver PAD is coming up.
start_calls.lunar_orbit: {csm}, Houston. You're in a 60-mile orbit, GO for the ten revs. Your TEI PAD comes on the last.
start_calls.tei: {csm}, Houston. Your TEI PAD is on its way up.
start_calls.transearth_coast: Houston: TEI was good. Your midcourse PAD will come up to trim the entry corridor.
start_calls.entry: Houston: entry interface in about twenty minutes. P61, CM/SM SEP when P62 asks, ELS LOGIC and AUTO.
start_calls._comment: CAPCOM's word as each start phase begins, the simulator's own [adapted]

vehicles._comment: Apollo 8's vehicles where they differ from data/spacecraft.json's, Apollo 11's

mass._source: The mission report's mass properties (MSC-PA-R-69-1, Table A.6-I: the spacecraft 87,377 lb at TLI, the CSM 63,524 lb at its separation from the S-IVB, the CM 12,179 lb after CM/SM separation) and its propellant loads (section 6.14: the SPS's 40,836 lb, the SM RCS's 1,342.4 lb, the CM RCS's 245.3 lb) [published]; the S-IVB at its second ignition, 126,867 kg with 72,727 kg of propellant (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, section 7 and Table 7-11) [published]. From them [derived]: the CM dry of its RCS's propellant, the SM dry of its own and the SPS's, the test article in the adapter (LTA-B with the adapter, the payload in place of the LM: the spacecraft at TLI less the CSM), and the S-IVB dry with the Instrument Unit and residuals (the vehicle at ignition less the spacecraft and the propellant)

sps._source: The SPS's load, 40,836 lb (MSC-PA-R-69-1, section 6.11.2) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's [simplified: Apollo 8's ran some 4 s long in LOI on low thrust, ibid., section 6.11]

sm_rcs._source: The SM RCS's load, 1,342.4 lb in four quads (MSC-PA-R-69-1, section 6.14.2) [published]

cm_rcs._source: The CM RCS's load, 245.3 lb in two systems (MSC-PA-R-69-1, section 6.14.2) [published]

sivb._source: The J-2 in AS-503's second S-IVB burn, TLI: 897,548 N and 4,199.2 N s/kg at the standard time slice (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, Table 7-7), and 59,862 kg of LOX with 12,865 kg of LH2 at the second ignition (ibid., Table 7-11, the best estimates) [published; the thrust and the specific impulse held through the burn: simplified]

s_ic._source: AS-503's F-1s: 6,726.6 kN and an Isp of 263.94 s each reduced to sea level, the flight's reconstruction (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, Table 5-2) [published]; 7,992 kN each in vacuum at OECO, the peak 38.85 m/s2 on 822,829 kg over four engines [derived], the exit area the difference over the sea level's pressure [derived]; the propellant the vehicle's mass from holddown release to OECO (ibid., Table 21-9) [derived], the vacuum Isp that burns it by the flown OECO, 153.82 s [estimated]

s_ii._source: AS-503's second flight stage at the S-II's ignition, its aft interstage and launch escape system jettisoned, and 212,425 kg at its cutoff signal (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, Table 21-9) [published], the propellant between them [derived]; five J-2s at the high mixture ratio, 5,086,888 N on 1,224.4 kg/s 61 s after the start command, and 3,877,101 N at the low ratio after the shift, all five burning to the cutoff (ibid., section 6) [published], on the flow that burns the rest by the flown cutoff, 524.04 s [estimated]

s_ivb._source: AS-503's third flight stage at the S-IVB's first start command (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, Table 21-9); the J-2 in the first burn, 901,557 N on 214.46 kg/s (ibid., Table 7-2) [published]

saturn_v._source: AS-503, Apollo 8's Saturn V, where it differs from spacecraft.json's AS-506: at holddown arm release 2,781,694 kg (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, Table 21-9) [published]; its drag and its guidance failure's rate AS-506's [estimated]

calls.emr_shift: Just had the PU shift, I believe.

launch._comment: Apollo 8's launch from Launch Complex 39A (its coordinates as Apollo 11's) at 12:51:00 UTC on 21 December 1968, GET 0, on the first crewed Saturn V, AS-503 [published]. The start phase begins on the pad at start_get_s: guidance reference release at grr_get_s (-16.97 s), the S-IC's start sequence commanded at ignition_get_s (-8.89 s), all engines running by thrust_ok_get_s (-1.38 s), the holddown arms' release at release_get_s (0.27 s) and T1 at t1_get_s (0.67 s), to the tenth of a second (Saturn V launch vehicle flight evaluation report, AS-503, MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, the sequence of events) [published]. The Instrument Unit's boost program on its time bases as AS-503 flew it (ibid.) [published]: the S-IC's centre engine cutoff at T1 125.26 s (125.93 s), T2 there and the tilt arrest on it (145.50 s); T3 at the outboard engines' cutoff (153.82 s), which the propellant ends, then staging, the S-II's start, its aft interstage's (second plane) separation, the launch escape tower's jettison, the iterative guidance's start and the mixture ratio's shift (443.45 s); AS-503's S-II burned on all five engines to its cutoff, the centre engine's early cutoff coming in from AS-504; T4 at the S-II's cutoff (524.04 s), then staging and the S-IVB's ignition; T5 at the S-IVB's velocity cutoff (685 s), and insertion after it (694.98 s). The yaw away from the tower, the tilt's start (at 137 m, or T1 13 s), the attitude rate limit and the time-tilt pitch polynomial are SA-504's presettings, as Apollo 11's [estimated for AS-503, whose presettings aren't at hand; its roll and pitch began at 12.11 s, ibid.], toward the flight azimuth, 72.124 deg (ibid., section 4) [published]. The S-IVB loses parking_orbit_loss_kg of propellant, vented and burned, between its first cutoff and its second start: 128,021 kg at the coast's start, 126,965 kg at the second start command (ibid., the vehicle's mass history) [derived]; the simulator takes it off at insertion [simplified]. The calls are the flight's (Apollo Flight Journal, Apollo 8, launch and ascent to Earth orbit): Launch Control's count, Houston's (Collins) and Borman's [published; the count's ignition call shortened, and Borman's second plane Sep through garble: adapted]

calls: Mark. You have S-IVB to orbit capability. Over.
launch_aborts._comment: Apollo 8's launch abort modes, Apollo 11's (its mission.json's launch_aborts) on the same vehicles [estimated], at the times Houston marked them on Apollo 8's flight (Apollo Flight Journal, launch and ascent to Earth orbit) [published]: Mode I Bravo at 0:42, Mode I Charlie at 1:52, S-IVB to orbit capability at 6:05 and Mode IV at 9:49. Mode III from 8 s before the S-II's cutoff, as Apollo 11's came [estimated: Houston didn't call it]. The calls are Collins's [published]

parking_orbit._comment: Apollo 8's orbit at insertion, from the Saturn V flight evaluation report for AS-503 (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, Table 4-6): inclination 32.509 deg and descending node 42.415 deg east of Greenwich at range zero, insertion at 694.98 s at 32.649 N 53.292 W, 191.36 km [published], put in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The report's 185.18 x 184.41 km orbit is taken as circular [simplified]. The launch start phase flies AS-503 into it

launch_refsmmat._comment: The launch pad REFSMMAT, which Apollo 8 flew to the Moon (Apollo Flight Journal, day 3): X horizontal along the flight azimuth (72.124 deg, MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, section 4.1), Z down along Launch Complex 39A's vertical, Y = Z x X, each a stable member axis in the ICRF, from tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]

tli._comment: TLI's conic, as the flown TLI left the stack on it: C3 -1,478,917 m2/s2 and eccentricity 0.97553, in the plane of inclination 30.636 deg and descending node 38.983 deg east of Greenwich (MPR-SAT-FE-69-1, Table 4-7: at TLI, 10 s after the cutoff signal) [published]; the plane in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. Its perigee lay 0.43 of the way through the burn's 25.2 deg arc, from the states at ignition and TLI (MSC-PA-R-69-1, Table 5-II) [derived], where Apollo 11's lay half way. TLI aimed Apollo 8 at the Moon, 130.2 nmi below its surface at 69:13:58, for the S-IVB's slingshot past it once the spacecraft had gone; the separation maneuvers then took the spacecraft to 0.8 nmi at 69:01:03 and 458.1 nmi at 68:57:40 (MSC-PA-R-69-1, Table 5-III) [published]. Those can't all be had from TLI and the separations as flown, 1.1 and 7.7 ft/s radially up: the first moved the pericynthion's time 13 min, which a 1.1 ft/s burn can't, and the S-IVB, venting, carried the spacecraft until it separated [simplified: the venting isn't modelled]. So the RTCC plans TLI's ignition time and energy (Rtcc.plan_tli()) for the pericynthion after the separations, flying them as impulses (aim_after): 464.0 nmi at 69:01:20, where the report's state at the first midcourse correction's ignition (ibid., Table 5-II) passes the Moon in the simulator [derived], 6 nmi and 4 min from the report's own reckoning, and within the approach the flight had, which the first midcourse correction took into the lunar orbit's plane. The midcourse corrections then aim at pericynthion_alt_km in the plane of the lunar site's orbit, at pericynthion_get, where the second left it (65.8 nmi at 69:10:39, ibid., Table 5-III) [published]. earliest_get_s: 2:40:00, ahead of the S-IVB's restart preparation at 2:40:59.5 (ibid., Table 5-II)

loi._comment: LOI-1's targets: the PAD's 169.3 by 60.0 nmi at its TIG, 69:08:19.52 (Apollo Flight Journal, 67:19:05; flown 168.5 by 60.0 nmi, MSC-PA-R-69-1, section 5.5) [published], above the Moon's mean radius [simplified]. The RTCC solves the burn at that TIG (Rtcc.plan_loi()), 23 s before the burn centred on the pericynthion would start: LOI-1 left the spacecraft still descending, 0.79 deg down at its cutoff, the orbit's perilune some 16 deg on, where LOI-2 burned two revolutions later (ibid., Table 5-II) [published]

lunar_site._comment: Without a landing site, the lunar orbit's plane is set by the point its ground track came farthest south, at LOI-2's cutoff: the plane through where the mission report has the CSM at LOI-1's, LOI-2's and TEI's ignitions and cutoffs (MSC-PA-R-69-1, Table 5-II), 12.29 deg to the Moon's equator, within 0.2 deg of each [derived]. The RTCC's midcourse corrections and LOI-1 put the orbit in it

lunar_orbit._comment: Apollo 8's lunar orbit after LOI-2: 60.7 by 59.7 nmi from LOI-2's cutoff at 73:35:16, 11.66 deg S 159.79 deg E (MSC-PA-R-69-1, section 5.5 and Table 5-II), where the lunar_orbit start phase starts, the SPS having given 961 m/s in MCC-1, LOI-1 and LOI-2 (20.4, 2,997 and 134.8 ft/s, ibid.) [published]. LOI-2's PAD targets 60.7 by 60.6 nmi (Apollo Flight Journal, 71:56:33) [published]. The Moon's field took the orbit to 63.6 by 58.6 nmi by TEI (MSC-PA-R-69-1, section 5.5)

tei._comment: TEI onto Apollo 8's return: the TEI-10 PAD's 3,522.3 ft/s at 89:19:15.67, its N81 +3,518.6, -151.2, -52.0 ft/s, from which the RTCC starts its solve (Apollo Flight Journal, 87:41:19) [published]; entry interface came at 146:46:12.8, 20.83 deg N 179.89 deg W, 36,221 ft/s, 6.50 deg down, heading 121.57 deg east of north (MSC-PA-R-69-1, Table 5-V) [published]. That state, put in the simulator, is on a return inclined 37.16 deg to the equator with its vacuum perigee 35.5 km up (Rtcc.vacuum_perigee()) [derived]. The RTCC solves the burn at the flown TEI's time for that inclination, that entry interface and that corridor (Rtcc.plan_tei()), and the transearth midcourse corrections aim at the corridor too

entry._comment: Apollo 8's target, N61 in the final entry PAD at 145:11:42 (Apollo Flight Journal): 8.13 deg N, 165.03 deg W, 1,216.6 nmi from entry interface, with no P65 [published]. The ground uplinks it with the entry PAD (the timeline's entry_pad), and the entry start phase starts with it loaded

dispersions._comment: The seed the flight's dispersions are drawn from: the CSM's unmodelled forces (spacecraft.json "unmodelled"), once for the flight, and MSFN's tracking error ("msfn"), for each uplink

msfn._comment: The Manned Space Flight Network's tracking error in the CSM state vector the RTCC plans the CSM's PADs from and uplinks with them (P27): standard deviations in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down), by the body the CSM's orbit is about, Apollo 11's [estimated]

timeline._comment: Mission Control from TLI to the entry. Each entry happens once: at its GET ('get') if its condition ('when', a flight phase or one of the sequencer's) holds then; CAPCOM makes the call ('say') and the ground uplinks the PAD ('pad'): the RTCC's solution, a midcourse correction's at its TIG ('tig'), TEI's at the opportunity nearest 'near', or a maneuver the flight plan fixed ('n81_ft_s', LVLH, at 'tig'). The times, calls and TIGs are Apollo 8's [published: the Apollo Flight Journal: GO for TLI 2:27:22; the second separation maneuver recommended at 4:05:43, 8 ft/s radially up at 4:37:22; the MCC-1 PAD 9:58:29, TIG 10:59:58.30; the MCC-4 PAD 59:46:42, TIG 60:59:54.30, flown as the second; the LOI-1 PAD 67:19:05; GO for LOI 68:04:07; the LOI-2 PAD 71:56:33; GO for LOI-2 72:46:16; the TEI-10 PAD 87:41:19; GO for TEI 88:03:36; the MCC-5 PAD 102:43:35, TIG 103:59:52.86; MCC-6 for 122:00:00, scrubbed at 121:08:44 (0.6 ft/s), and MCC-7 for 144:46, scrubbed at 140:35:52, the corridor made without them; the final entry PAD 145:11:42; GO for pyro arm 146:26:57], except the entries marked estimated. The separation maneuvers from the S-IVB are the mission report's as flown, radially up: 1.1 ft/s at 3:40:01 and 7.7 ft/s at 4:45:01 (MSC-PA-R-69-1, sections 5.3 and 7.2.4) [published]
